channel.title: Lead Elite Academy Blog
channel.description: Brandon Thornhill, former Navy SEAL and creator of Lead Elite Academy, on building leaders, standards and systems that run without you.

item.title: We Bought a $50K Sales Course and Nobody Used It
item.description: Why the training your company paid for never stuck, and what has to exist around a program before anything will.

item.title: Why "Be More Disciplined" Has Never Fixed a Team
item.description: Discipline is a personal solution to an organizational problem. What a former Navy SEAL got wrong about it, and what a leader has to build to get it at scale.

item.title: You Promoted Your Best Producer. Who Taught Them to Lead?
item.description: Selling is a skill and leading is a different skill. Why most managers were never taught the second one, and what it costs the people under them.

item.title: The Four Tests of a System
item.description: A five-minute check any leader can run on their own building to find out whether they have a system or a manager doing everything alone.

item.title: Why Every Problem Ends Up on Your Desk
item.description: When a leadership team is buried in questions their people could have answered, the cause is usually something the leaders trained without meaning to.

item.title: What You Allow Becomes Your Culture
item.description: Casualness never shows up in the numbers first. A lesson from Afghanistan on how standards slip while the results still look good.

item.title: Why Lead Elite Academy Runs 52 Weeks
item.description: Fifty-two weeks sounds like a long commitment. What a week actually asks of a leader, and why the year is the point.
